0.title: Glorifying God Together
0.overview:
Worship is what we were made for. The first question of an old catechism asks, "What is the chief end of man?" and answers, "Man's chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him forever." Every human being worships something. The question is never whether we will worship, but what, and how.

Yet worship has become one of the most debated subjects in the church. Some think of it mainly as music. Others argue about styles, instruments, lighting and length. Some treat Sunday as a day like any other; others as a day of strict rules. Behind these practical questions lie deeper ones. What is worship? Who decides how God should be worshipped? What should happen when the church gathers? And what is the Lord's Day for?

Jesus said, the hour is coming, and is now here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father is seeking such people to worship him (John 4:23). God is not only worthy of worship; he seeks worshippers. That is an invitation.

Six units: (1) What Is Worship?; (2) Worshipping God His Way; (3) What Happens When the Church Gathers; (4) Singing to the Lord; (5) The Lord's Day; (6) Worship with All of Life. Two questions are handled with the main views and a verdict: how Scripture governs worship (Unit 2) and how the Sabbath applies to Christians (Unit 5).

1.title: What Is Worship?
1.overview:
Worship is giving God the honour he deserves. The word "worship" in English comes from "worth-ship." To worship God is to declare and treat him as supremely worthy. In Scripture, worship includes bowing down, serving, praising, thanking and offering. It is both an attitude of the heart and acts of the body and voice.

Worship is a response. We do not worship to get God's attention. We worship because he has revealed himself and acted. Oh come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD, our Maker! For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture (Ps 95:6-7). Worship always begins with who God is and what he has done. That is why worship and Scripture belong together.

Worship is in spirit and truth. Jesus told the Samaritan woman that place was no longer the issue. Not this mountain or Jerusalem, but in spirit and truth (John 4:23-24). Worship must be in spirit: from the heart, by the Holy Spirit, not mere outward form. And worship must be in truth: according to God's revealed truth, and centred on Christ, who is the truth. Hearts without truth produce sincere idolatry. Truth without hearts produces dead orthodoxy. God wants both.

Worship is through Christ. We cannot approach a holy God on our own. Christ is our great high priest, and through him we have access to the Father. Through him then let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God (Heb 13:15). Every Christian prayer and song goes to the Father through the Son by the Spirit.

Worship is all of life and also gathered. Paul says presenting our bodies as living sacrifices is our spiritual worship (Rom 12:1). All of life can be worship. But Scripture also calls God's people to gather for worship. These are not rivals. The gathered worship of Sunday shapes the scattered worship of Monday, and the whole week of obedience flows back into Sunday praise.
1.theology:
Worship and idolatry: The opposite of true worship is not no worship but idolatry. Human hearts are idol factories. We worship money, comfort, approval, success or family when we look to them for what only God can give. True worship dethrones these idols.

The audience of worship: In gathered worship, God is the audience, and the whole congregation are participants. Leaders and musicians are not performers for a crowd but servants helping the people worship together.

Reverence and joy: Scripture calls for both. Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling (Ps 2:11). Worship that is only joyful becomes shallow; worship that is only solemn becomes cold.
1.examples:
Then: When Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up, he heard the seraphim crying, Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts, and he cried out, Woe is me! For I am lost (Isa 6:3, 5). After his lips were cleansed, he answered God's call: Here I am! Send me (Isa 6:8). True worship moves from seeing God, to confession, to forgiveness, to obedience.

Now: A man has always judged Sunday services by whether he "got something out of it." Studying worship, he realises he has made himself the audience. He begins to come to church asking a different question: "How can I give God the praise he deserves, and help others to do the same?" Strangely, he now gets far more out of it.

A simple test: Before church next Sunday, ask yourself: am I going mainly to receive something, or mainly to give God glory?

verseByVerse.quote: Oh come, let us sing to the LORD; let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation! Let us come into his presence with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise to him with songs of praise! For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the depths of the earth; the heights of the mountains are his also. The sea is his, for he made it, and his hands formed the dry land. Oh come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD, our Maker! For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. Today, if you hear his voice, (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This psalm is a call to worship that has been used by God's people for centuries. It begins with joyful noise and thanksgiving, grounded in God's greatness as Creator. Then it moves to bowing and kneeling, grounded in his covenant care: we are the people of his pasture. The psalm continues with a warning not to harden our hearts (Ps 95:8). Worship must reach the heart.

verseByVerse.quote: Jesus said to her, "Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father. You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews. But the hour is coming, and is now here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father is seeking such people to worship him. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Samaritan woman raised a question about the right place of worship. Jesus moved the conversation from place to person. The hour has come when true worshippers worship the Father in spirit and truth. And notice: the Father is seeking such worshippers. Worship is not our attempt to find God. It is our response to the God who has found us.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore let us be grateful for receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, and thus let us offer to God acceptable worship, with reverence and awe, for our God is a consuming fire. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Believers have received an unshakeable kingdom. The right response is gratitude, and gratitude takes the form of acceptable worship, with reverence and awe. The reason is sobering: our God is a consuming fire. The God of grace is still the God of Sinai. Gratitude and awe belong together.

verseByVerse.quote: Through him then let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name. Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Animal sacrifices have ended in Christ, but Christian worship still has sacrifices. One is the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name. The other is doing good and sharing with others. Praise without kindness is empty. Both are pleasing to God.

1.reflection:
What is your own definition of worship after reading this unit?

Why must worship be both "in spirit" and "in truth"?

What idols compete with God for your worship?

How could you prepare your heart for gathered worship this Sunday?

2.title: Worshipping God His Way
2.overview:
Can we worship God however we like, as long as we are sincere? Scripture says no. God cares not only that he is worshipped, but how.

Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them. Fire came from the LORD and consumed them. Moses explained: Among those who are near me I will be sanctified, and before all the people I will be glorified (Lev 10:1-3). They were priests, at the right place, offering to the right God. But they did it in a way he had not commanded.

The second commandment forbids making images to worship God, even images meant to honour him (Exod 20:4-6). The golden calf was presented as the LORD who brought them out of Egypt (Exod 32:4-5), yet it was idolatry. God told Israel, Everything that I command you, you shall be careful to do. You shall not add to it or take from it (Deut 12:32). Jesus rebuked the Pharisees for worship that taught as doctrines the commandments of men (Matt 15:9).

The principle is clear: God is the one who decides how he is to be approached. We do not invent worship; we receive it. This is a protection as well as a restriction. It frees churches from the endless pressure to innovate, and it frees worshippers from having their consciences bound by human inventions.

What has God commanded for gathered worship? The New Testament shows the essential elements: the reading of Scripture (1 Tim 4:13), preaching (2 Tim 4:2), prayer (1 Tim 2:1), singing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs (Col 3:16), baptism and the Lord's Supper (Matt 28:19; 1 Cor 11:23-26), giving (1 Cor 16:2) and the confession of faith. These are the heart of Christian worship in every culture and age.
2.theology:
Regulating worship: the views. The "normative principle," held by Lutherans, Anglicans and many evangelicals, says that anything not forbidden in Scripture may be included in worship. The "regulative principle," held by the Reformed tradition, says that only what Scripture commands or warrants may be included as an element of worship.

The verdict: The regulative principle best fits Leviticus 10, Deuteronomy 12:32 and Jesus' rebuke in Matthew 15. But it must be applied with wisdom. It governs the elements of worship (what we do). It does not dictate the circumstances (when, where, how long, what building, what tune), which are ordered by wisdom and decency (1 Cor 14:40). Drama, liturgical dance and religious images are additions; a sound system and a printed order of service are circumstances.

Musical instruments: Some who hold the regulative principle exclude instruments, seeing them as part of temple worship that ended with Christ. But the Psalms, which the church is told to sing, repeatedly call for instruments (Ps 150), and they are heard in heavenly worship (Rev 5:8). Instruments that serve congregational singing are a legitimate help. They must support the singing, not replace or drown it.
2.examples:
Then: King Uzziah was a strong and successful king, but when he grew proud he entered the temple to burn incense, a task God had given only to the priests. He was struck with leprosy (2 Chr 26:16-21). Even a king could not invent his own approach to God.

Now: A church leadership team feels under pressure to make the service more exciting with a drama, video clips and a short message. They study Scripture together and decide instead to give more time to Bible reading, congregational prayer and singing. Some visitors find it plain at first. But over time members say they have never felt closer to God in worship.

A simple test: When you evaluate worship, do you ask first "Was it moving?" or "Was it what God has asked for?"

verseByVerse.quote: Now Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his censer and put fire in it and laid incense on it and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them. And fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD. Then Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD has said: 'Among those who are near me I will be sanctified, and before all the people I will be glorified.'" And Aaron held his peace. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This shocking event happened at the very start of Israel's priesthood. Nadab and Abihu had seen God's glory on Sinai (Exod 24:9-11). Yet they offered fire God had not commanded. God's response teaches that he is holy and must be approached on his terms. Aaron's silence is striking. He did not argue, because God's word was clear.

verseByVerse.quote: "When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations whom you go in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and dwell in their land, take care that you be not ensnared to follow them, after they have been destroyed before you, and that you do not inquire about their gods, saying, 'How did these nations serve their gods?—that I also may do the same.' You shall not worship the LORD your God in that way, for every abominable thing that the LORD hates they have done for their gods, for they even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire to their gods. "Everything that I command you, you shall be careful to do. You shall not add to it or take from it. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: As Israel entered Canaan, they would be tempted to worship the LORD the way the nations worshipped their gods. Moses forbids it. God's people must not borrow pagan practices, even with good intentions. And they must neither add to nor take away from what God has commanded. Worship is to be shaped by God's word, not by surrounding culture.

verseByVerse.quote: You hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, when he said: "'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; in vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.'" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus quotes Isaiah to rebuke religious leaders whose traditions had overridden God's commands. Their lips honoured God but their hearts were far from him. And their worship was in vain because it taught human commandments as if they were God's. Sincere-looking worship can still be empty.

verseByVerse.quote: What then, brothers? When you come together, each one has a hymn, a lesson, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Let all things be done for building up. If any speak in a tongue, let there be only two or at most three, and each in turn, and let someone interpret. But if there is no one to interpret, let each of them keep silent in church and speak to himself and to God. Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said. If a revelation is made to another sitting there, let the first be silent. For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all be encouraged, and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets. For God is not a God of confusion but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints, (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Corinthian gatherings were chaotic. Paul gives instructions: everything for building up, speakers in turn, silence when needed. The reason is theological: For God is not a God of confusion but of peace. Orderly worship reflects the character of God. Freedom in worship is never freedom from order.

2.reflection:
Why do you think God cares about how he is worshipped, not only that he is worshipped?

What is the difference between an element and a circumstance of worship?

Is there anything in your church's worship that comes more from tradition or culture than from Scripture?

How does the regulative principle protect worshippers' consciences?

3.title: What Happens When the Church Gathers
3.overview:
Gathered worship is a meeting between God and his people. In it, God speaks to us and we respond to him. Seeing worship as a dialogue helps us understand each part.

God calls us. Worship begins with God's invitation, often a call to worship from Scripture. We do not come on our own initiative but because he summons us.

We confess our sin. Coming before a holy God, we acknowledge our sin and hear his assurance of forgiveness in Christ (1 John 1:9). This keeps worship humble and grace-centred.

God speaks through his word. The public reading of Scripture and the preaching of the word are the centre of Christian worship. Paul told Timothy, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, to teaching (1 Tim 4:13). Preaching is not a lecture or a pep talk. It is God speaking through a messenger, explaining his word and applying it to his people. Preach the word; be ready in season and out of season (2 Tim 4:2).

We pray. The gathered church prays for its members, for the lost, for rulers and for the spread of the gospel (1 Tim 2:1-2). Congregational prayer is one of the most neglected parts of worship today.

We sing. Through song, believers praise God and teach one another (Col 3:16).

We give. Giving is an act of worship, an offering of thanks to God and a sharing with those in need (2 Cor 9:12-13).

God seals his promises. In baptism and the Lord's Supper, God confirms his promises to believers in visible signs.

God blesses us. Worship often ends with a benediction, God's blessing spoken over his people as they go out, such as The LORD bless you and keep you (Num 6:24).

The shape may vary from church to church. But the elements are the same, and the movement from God's word to our response is constant.
3.theology:
The priority of preaching: Faith comes by hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ (Rom 10:17). Preaching is God's chosen means for saving sinners and building up his church. A church that marginalises preaching in favour of other activities has misplaced the centre.

Participation: In New Testament worship, the congregation is not passive. Everyone sings, prays (at least by saying "Amen") and listens actively. Paul expects outsiders to be able to say "Amen" to what is said (1 Cor 14:16).

Accessible to outsiders: Worship is for believers, but outsiders may come in. Paul wanted them to understand and be convicted, so that falling on his face, he will worship God and declare that God is really among you (1 Cor 14:25). Clarity serves the gospel.
3.examples:
Then: After the exile, Ezra read the Law to the gathered people from early morning until midday. The Levites gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading (Neh 8:8). The people wept, then celebrated, because they had understood the words. This is the root of expository preaching.

Now: A Christian used to arrive late and leave right after the sermon. Learning that worship is a dialogue with God, he begins to come early, pray for the service, listen to the Scripture reading as God's voice and stay for the benediction. Worship becomes the high point of his week.

A simple test: During the sermon, are you listening for information, or for God's word to you?

verseByVerse.quote: And all the people gathered as one man into the square before the Water Gate. And they told Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses that the LORD had commanded Israel. So Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly, both men and women and all who could understand what they heard, on the first day of the seventh month. And he read from it facing the square before the Water Gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women and those who could understand. And the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Law. And Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that they had made for the purpose. And beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right hand, and Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam on his left hand. And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was above all the people, and as he opened it all the people stood. And Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," lifting up their hands. And they bowed their heads and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground. Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, the Levites, helped the people to understand the Law, while the people remained in their places. They read from the book, from the Law of God, clearly, and they gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The whole people gathered and asked Ezra to bring the Book of the Law. They stood as it was opened, worshipped, and listened attentively. Levites helped the people understand. This scene shows the reverence due to God's word in worship, and the need for it to be explained, not only read.

verseByVerse.quote: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, to teaching. Do not neglect the gift you have, which was given you by prophecy when the council of elders laid their hands on you. Practice these things, immerse yourself in them, so that all may see your progress. Keep a close watch on yourself and on the teaching. Persist in this, for by so doing you will save both yourself and your hearers. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul gives Timothy three tasks for his public ministry: reading, exhorting and teaching. Then he urges him to watch his life and doctrine, because by doing so he will save himself and his hearers. The public reading and preaching of Scripture is a matter of life and death.

verseByVerse.quote: I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom: preach the word; be ready in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort, with complete patience and teaching. For the time is coming when people will not endure sound teaching, but having itching ears they will accumulate for themselves teachers to suit their own passions, and will turn away from listening to the truth and wander off into myths. As for you, always be sober-minded, endure suffering, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul's charge is solemn: in the presence of God and Christ the Judge. Preach the word. Reprove, rebuke, exhort, with patience. The reason is that people will want teachers who tell them what they want to hear. The preacher's job is not to be popular but faithful.

verseByVerse.quote: First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and all who are in high positions, that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way. This is good, and it is pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The first thing Paul urges for the gathered church is prayer of every kind, for all people, including rulers. The aim is a peaceful life and the salvation of the lost. God desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. Congregational prayer has a missionary heart.

3.reflection:
How does thinking of worship as a dialogue between God and his people change your view of the service?

Why is preaching central to Christian worship?

How could your church give more attention to congregational prayer?

Which part of gathered worship do you find hardest to engage with? Why?

4.title: Singing to the Lord
4.overview:
The Bible is full of singing. Moses and Miriam sang after the Red Sea. David wrote psalms. Jesus and his disciples sang a hymn after the Last Supper (Matt 26:30). Paul and Silas sang in prison at midnight (Acts 16:25). And the book of Revelation rings with songs before the throne. God's people are a singing people.

Why we sing. Singing joins truth and emotion. It engages the mind, the heart and the body. It helps us remember what we believe. And it unites a congregation: many voices become one praise.

Singing to God and to one another. Paul describes singing as both upward and outward: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom, singing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, with thankfulness in your hearts to God (Col 3:16). When we sing, we praise God and also teach each other. That means the words matter. A song that is musically beautiful but theologically empty does not teach well.

What makes a good song for worship? It is true to Scripture. It focuses on God and his works, not mainly on our feelings. It is singable by a congregation, not only by a soloist. It has enough depth to bear repetition and to carry people through suffering. And it is sung from the heart.

Singing the Psalms. The Psalms are God's own songbook, inspired by the Spirit. They cover every human emotion: praise, thanksgiving, confession, lament, anger, trust and hope. Churches that never sing psalms lose the language of lament and the honesty of the psalmists. A church that rediscovers the Psalms will find its prayers and songs deepened.

The song of heaven. In Revelation, the redeemed sing a new song to the Lamb: Worthy are you to take the scroll and to open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you ransomed people for God from every tribe and language and people and nation (Rev 5:9). Our singing now is rehearsal for that day.
4.theology:
Only psalms? The views. Some Reformed churches sing only the biblical Psalms in worship (exclusive psalmody), reasoning that only inspired songs should be sung. Most churches sing psalms alongside hymns and songs written by believers.

The verdict: Paul's phrase psalms and hymns and spiritual songs (Col 3:16; Eph 5:19) most naturally refers to a variety of songs, and the New Testament itself contains Christ-centred hymns (Phil 2:6-11; Col 1:15-20; Rev 5:9-10). The church may sing faithful songs that celebrate Christ by name. But exclusive psalmody reminds us of something important: the Psalms should have a large place in our singing.

Music styles: Scripture does not prescribe a musical style. Churches should choose music that serves congregational singing and fits the words, and members should bear with one another's preferences in love.
4.examples:
Then: In a Philippian jail, beaten and in stocks, Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them (Acts 16:25). Their singing in suffering was itself a witness.

Now: An elderly woman with dementia can no longer recognise her family. But when her pastor visits and begins to sing a hymn she has known since childhood, she sings every verse with him. The truths she sang for decades have been stored deeper than her memory can reach.

A simple test: Look at the words of the songs you sang last Sunday. What did they teach you about God?

verseByVerse.quote: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom, singing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, with thankfulness in your hearts to God. And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Singing is one way the word of Christ dwells richly in a church. It teaches and admonishes, it expresses thankfulness and it is directed to God. Paul then widens the circle: whatever you do, in word or deed, do it in the name of the Lord Jesus. Sunday singing and weekday living are both worship.

verseByVerse.quote: And do not get drunk with wine, for that is debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit, addressing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody to the Lord with your heart, giving thanks always and for everything to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, submitting to one another out of reverence for Christ. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Being filled with the Spirit shows itself in singing, thanksgiving and mutual submission. Notice that the singing is addressing one another and also making melody to the Lord with your heart. A Spirit-filled church is a singing church.

verseByVerse.quote: Oh sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth! Sing to the LORD, bless his name; tell of his salvation from day to day. Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples! For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The call to sing to the LORD a new song reaches out to all the earth. Singing is missionary: Declare his glory among the nations. When the church sings God's praise, it proclaims his greatness to the world. The psalm ends with all creation rejoicing at the Lord's coming to judge in righteousness.

verseByVerse.quote: And they sang a new song, saying, "Worthy are you to take the scroll and to open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you ransomed people for God from every tribe and language and people and nation, and you have made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they shall reign on the earth." Then I looked, and I heard around the throne and the living creatures and the elders the voice of many angels, numbering myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands, saying with a loud voice, "Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and wealth and wisdom and might and honor and glory and blessing!" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The new song in heaven celebrates the Lamb who was slain. Its subject is redemption: people ransomed from every nation, made a kingdom and priests. Then the circle widens to myriads of angels. The song of heaven is about Christ and his cross. If that is the song of eternity, it should be the centre of our songs now.

4.reflection:
Why do you think God wants his people to sing, not only to speak?

Choose a favourite song or hymn. What does it teach about God?

How could you make more use of the Psalms in your singing and praying?

Read Revelation 5:9-14. How should the song of heaven shape our singing now?

5.title: The Lord's Day
5.overview:
From the beginning, God built a rhythm into creation. He worked six days and rested on the seventh, and God blessed the seventh day and made it holy (Gen 2:3). In the Ten Commandments he commanded Israel to keep the Sabbath day holy, resting from work as he had rested (Exod 20:8-11). In Deuteronomy, the Sabbath also recalled their rescue from slavery in Egypt: slaves get no rest, but God's freed people do (Deut 5:15).

Christ and the Sabbath. Jesus called himself lord even of the Sabbath and said, The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath (Mark 2:27-28). He healed on the Sabbath and rejected the Pharisees' burdensome rules. And he offered something the Sabbath only pictured: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest (Matt 11:28). The true Sabbath rest is found in him.

Sabbath fulfilled in Christ. Paul writes, Therefore let no one pass judgment on you in questions of food and drink, or with regard to a festival or a new moon or a Sabbath. These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ (Col 2:16-17). Hebrews says that a Sabbath rest remains for God's people, entered by faith in Christ and completed in glory (Heb 4:9-10). The weekly Sabbath was a shadow; Christ is the reality.

The Lord's Day. The early church gathered on the first day of the week, the day of the resurrection (Acts 20:7; 1 Cor 16:2). John calls it the Lord's day (Rev 1:10). It is not the Jewish Sabbath moved to Sunday with all its regulations. It is the day of new creation, when the risen Christ meets his people.

Rest as a gift. The principle of rest remains wise and good. Human beings are not machines. A regular rhythm of rest is a gift from our Creator and an act of trust: we stop working because God, not we, holds the world together. Sunday, set apart for worship, fellowship and rest, is a great blessing to be enjoyed rather than a law to be feared.
5.theology:
The Sabbath and Christians: the views. Many Reformed Christians hold that the fourth commandment is a moral law for all time, so that Sunday is "the Christian Sabbath," to be kept holy by rest from ordinary work and recreation. Others hold that the Sabbath was part of the Mosaic covenant, a sign for Israel (Exod 31:13), fulfilled in Christ, so that Christians are not bound by a weekly Sabbath law, though they gather on the Lord's Day.

The verdict: The Sabbath is fulfilled in Christ. Colossians 2:16-17 calls it a shadow, and Romans 14:5-6 lets believers differ over days. Of the Ten Commandments, the Sabbath alone is not repeated as a command in the New Testament. Yet the gathering of the church on the Lord's Day is the clear apostolic pattern and must not be neglected (Heb 10:25), and the rhythm of rest that God built into creation remains wise.

No judging: Christians who keep Sunday as a Sabbath and those who do not should not judge one another (Rom 14:4-6). Both should honour the Lord's Day with gathered worship.
5.examples:
Then: On the first day of the week at Troas, the church gathered to break bread, and Paul talked with them until midnight. A young man fell asleep, fell from a window and was taken up dead, and Paul restored him to life (Acts 20:7-12). The Lord's Day gathering was so precious that it lasted all night.

Now: A family has filled Sundays with sports, errands and work emails, squeezing in church when they can. They decide to treat Sunday as a gift: church in the morning, a long family lunch, a walk, time with friends, no work email. They do not make it a list of rules. But they find their whole week steadier because it now begins with worship and rest.

A simple test: Does your Sunday look different from your other days? Does it point you to Christ, your true rest?

verseByVerse.quote: "Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days you shall labor, and do all your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work, you, or your son, or your daughter, your male servant, or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates. For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The fourth commandment grounds the Sabbath in creation: God worked six days and rested on the seventh. Rest extended to everyone in the household, including servants, foreigners and animals. It was a day for remembering that the world belongs to God, and that his people are not slaves.

verseByVerse.quote: One Sabbath he was going through the grainfields, and as they made their way, his disciples began to pluck heads of grain. And the Pharisees were saying to him, "Look, why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?" And he said to them, "Have you never read what David did, when he was in need and was hungry, he and those who were with him: how he entered the house of God, in the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the bread of the Presence, which it is not lawful for any but the priests to eat, and also gave it to those who were with him?" And he said to them, "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath. So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Pharisees accused Jesus' disciples of breaking the Sabbath by picking grain. Jesus answered with David's example and then with two great claims. The Sabbath was made for man's good, not as a burden. And the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath. The one who made the Sabbath has authority to interpret it, and to fulfil it.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore let no one pass judgment on you in questions of food and drink, or with regard to a festival or a new moon or a Sabbath. These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: False teachers in Colossae were judging believers for not keeping food laws and holy days, including Sabbaths. Paul says these were shadows; the substance is Christ. A shadow is real, but it points to something greater. Now that the substance has come, believers should not be judged by the shadow.

verseByVerse.quote: So then, there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God, for whoever has entered God's rest has also rested from his works as God did from his. Let us therefore strive to enter that rest, so that no one may fall by the same sort of disobedience. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The writer argues that God's rest was not finally given in Joshua's day. A Sabbath rest remains for God's people, entered by ceasing from our own works and trusting Christ. It will be completed in glory. Every Lord's Day is a foretaste of that eternal rest.

5.reflection:
What does the Sabbath in creation teach us about God and about ourselves?

How does Jesus fulfil the Sabbath?

How can Christians who hold different views on the Sabbath avoid judging one another?

What would it look like for you to receive the Lord's Day as a gift this week?

6.title: Worship with All of Life
6.overview:
Gathered worship matters, but it is not the whole of worship. I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship (Rom 12:1). The whole of life, offered to God, is worship.

Worship that God rejects. The prophets warned that worship without obedience is offensive to God. Amos heard God say, I hate, I despise your feasts, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies, because the people who worshipped were oppressing the poor. God wanted instead justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream (Amos 5:21, 24). Isaiah and Micah said the same. Songs on Sunday mean little if our lives deny them on Monday.

Worship in ordinary life. So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God (1 Cor 10:31). Work, family life, rest, hospitality, friendship and service can all be done to God's glory. The farmer, the nurse, the parent and the student can offer their days as worship.

Worship in suffering. Job, having lost everything, fell on the ground and worshiped and said, blessed be the name of the LORD (Job 1:20-21). Worship in suffering is perhaps the purest worship of all, because it honours God for who he is, not for what he gives.

Worship forever. Worship is not a temporary activity. It is the eternal occupation of the redeemed. In the new creation, the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will worship him. They will see his face (Rev 22:3-4). Everything in our worship now, gathered and scattered, is preparation for that day.
6.theology:
Worship and ethics: True worship and holy living are inseparable. The same Spirit who leads us to praise God leads us to love our neighbour. Worship that does not change how we live is not true worship.

Worship and mission: Mission exists because worship does not. The goal of evangelism is to bring more worshippers to God from every nation (Rom 15:9-11). When the church worships, it shows the world what it was made for.

Not everything is equally worship: While all of life can be worship, the gathered worship of the church has a special place. It is where God has promised to meet his people through word and sacrament. The truth that all of life is worship should never become a reason to neglect the gathered church.
6.examples:
Then: Daniel, a senior official in Babylon, continued to pray three times a day toward Jerusalem even when it became a crime punishable by death (Dan 6:10). His daily work in a pagan government and his worship of God were not separate. His faithfulness in both gave him courage when tested.

Now: A nurse working night shifts often misses Sunday services. She feels her faith is weak because her worship life seems thin. Her pastor reminds her that caring for the sick, done for Christ, is worship, and helps her find a midweek Bible study and a way to attend church at least twice a month. She begins to see her work as an offering.

A simple test: If someone watched your life this week, would they see a worshipper of God?

verseByVerse.quote: I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship. Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul begins the practical part of Romans with worship. The motive is the mercies of God described in chapters 1 to 11. The offering is our bodies, our whole selves. And the means is transformation by the renewing of our minds, rather than conformity to the world. Worship is a whole life reshaped by grace.

verseByVerse.quote: "I hate, I despise your feasts, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies. Even though you offer me your burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; and the peace offerings of your fattened animals, I will not look upon them. Take away from me the noise of your songs; to the melody of your harps I will not listen. But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God speaks with shocking bluntness. He hates the feasts, rejects the offerings and will not listen to the songs. Why? Because worshippers were trampling the poor. God does not want religion instead of righteousness. He wants justice and righteousness flowing like a river that never runs dry.

verseByVerse.quote: So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul writes this after a long discussion of food offered to idols. Even something as ordinary as eating and drinking can glorify God. The principle covers whatever you do. No part of life is too small or too secular to be offered to God.

verseByVerse.quote: Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb through the middle of the street of the city; also, on either side of the river, the tree of life with its twelve kinds of fruit, yielding its fruit each month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. No longer will there be anything accursed, but the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will worship him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. And night will be no more. They will need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light, and they will reign forever and ever. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Bible ends where it began, in a garden with the tree of life, but now a city too. The curse is gone. God's servants worship him and see his face. All of history moves toward this: the face-to-face worship of God and the Lamb, forever.

6.reflection:
What does it mean to present your body as a living sacrifice?

Read Amos 5:21-24. What might God say about the gap between our Sunday worship and our weekday lives?

How can your work, family life or rest be offered to God as worship this week?

How does the promise of Revelation 22:3-4 shape your worship now?
